items.title: A quasi-compact morphism is dominant exactly when it hits the generic point of every irreducible component of the target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a quasi-compact morphism is dominant exactly when the generic point of every irreducible component of the target lies in its image (statement lines 1271-1280). The counted proof is a short reduction to the affine case: quasi-compactness lets one cover the preimage of an affine open by finitely many affines, whose disjoint union is again affine, and dominance as well as the relevant generic points are unaffected by this replacement, after which the affine algebra criterion applies (proof lines 1282-1302). It is H2: the reduction is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the affineness of finite disjoint unions and the affine criterion.
